parameters.appliesAt: |lat| >= about 45 S in the summer months
parameters.fajrFormula: fajr = sunrise - 0.3063 N, for the whole month
parameters.nightDefinition: N = sunrise(d) - sunset(d-1), the previous night
parameters.portionMeaning: 18.38/60 and 16.68/60 of the night, NOT adhan's angle/60
parameters.handover: the two columns switch on different days: fajr month-wide, isha hands over over 3-4 November - the angle branch is the only fit on 1-2 November (it is later than the portion by 4.8 and 1.8 min), 3 November is inside a minute on both (0.87 angle, 0.42 portion) and is not separable, and the portion wins on every day from 4 November
parameters.seasonality: the branch is seasonal: July 2025 and the Octobers are pure angle, and the seam sits at the workbook boundary

highLatitude.provenance: T-668 #6966 (Punta Arenas at 53 S fully characterised; the publisher runs the fajr branch on every day of the month, including days where the 18 degree angle still exists) and #6991 (C43: both constants reproduce to 0.0002/0.0003, the every-day test passes 30/30 with the portion residual never over 0.79 min while the angle residual runs to +93.41 min on the sixteen days the 18 degree fajr still exists - so the branch is measurable from 1 November, not only after the angle fails. The corrected claim is the crossover, one day wide and sub-minute)

rollover.rule: a 00:xx isha belongs to the previous civil date
rollover.belongsToDate: the prayer's own astronomical date, not the civil date printed
rollover.notTruncation: the November 23:59 values are the last month the isha fits inside its own date, not a clip
rollover.provenance: T-668 #6966 (archived Decembers print post-midnight isha as 00:xx on its own date's row)

evidence.fullYearBasis: T-668 #6966: November and October for all 18 cities (a 30/31-day pair), validated 0 mismatches against C7's independent captures. No full year exists on the publisher's site
evidence.gradeBasis: Recipe-tier with a polar branch: one recipe reproduces 540 November and 558 October rows across 34.7 degrees of latitude, seventeen cities within 2 min. Single published cycle only, so it cannot reach grade A (#6943)

gaps: No multi-year path from the publisher: uploads are purged and year slugs 404. Wayback holds 190 PDFs across five years in three naming eras, but no contiguous run, so the series must be built forward month by month.
Ten months of the annual cycle are unmeasured: only October and November are captured.
The polar branch's seam dates are known only for the captured months; where it switches in a different year is unverified.
The 18 city coordinates are in the C17 archive, not in this object.
notes: Publishing defects on record: the Vina del Mar button links October's sheet while November exists unlinked, and December publishes around 29 November.
This is the census's only publisher spanning 34.7 degrees of latitude with a stated branch, so it is the practical test case for the app's high-latitude display policy.

gaps: The served table is FROZEN: the year parameter relabels dates and recomputes weekdays, changing nothing else, so all 13 columns are byte-identical across years. Against adhan per year the non-leap years score ~79 pc exact and leap years ~68 pc, within-1 staying 96.7-98.5 pc.
The table is locked to one leap phase and emits a phantom 29-Feb row dated 1 March in non-leap years, which the site's JavaScript deletes client-side.
Local variants exist: Isipingo Beach carries ishraaq +20, Phuthaditjhaba and Witsieshoek carry a Drakensberg elevation horizon correction, and Blantyre's anchor offset is unexplained.
Country assignment came from a boundary file with the label suffix first, so the 23-country count includes three Saudi towns and outriders in twelve further countries.
The zawaal row (transit - 5) is a seventh derived column the schema has no key for; zuhr = zawaal + 10 follows from it.
notes: One federation object with the town table, not one object per country: the margins are town-invariant and the country is a property of the town row. This is the judgement the brief asked to be documented.
A related keyless API (Salaah Times, 486 towns, 20 countries) transcribes Jamiat towns verbatim plus BMA, which makes it a mirror rather than a second authority.
